DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Building, EDSA corncr Quezon Avenue, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT HON. LOURDES S. CATAQUIZ City Mayor City of San Pedro, Laguna Dear Mayor Cataquiz: DILG Legal Opinion No. 50 S. 2015 28 DEC 2015 We write concerning your 23 September 2015 letter requesting that you be empowered to appoint the barangay officials of the seven (7) newly created barangays in a temporary capacity until the next barangay elections. Based on the records, the approval for the creation of seven (7) new barangays as separate and distinct barangays from its mother barangay, Barangay San Vicente, Municipality of San Pedro, Lagunal, was made pursuant Laguna Provincial Ordinance No. 8, s. 1997. The creation of these seven (7) new barangays was ratified in a plebiscite held on 11 July 2015. On 13 July 2015, the City of San Pedro formally requested the Commission on Elections (hereinafter, the "Commission") that an election be held for the purpose. However, the Commission denied said request primarily in consideration of the preparations for the upcoming May 2016 National and Local Elections. It is your position that the Commission's denial will adversely affect the delivery of basic services and public accountability for the funds and programs in these barangays. Hence, this request. Power of the City Ma yor to Appoint The power of the City Mayor to appoint is provided under Section 455 (b) (I) of Republic Act No. 7160 (hereinafter, the "Code"), which provides as follows: "Section 455. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties and Compensation. —xxx (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of 70hich is the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the city mayor shall: On 28 December 2013, the conversion of the Municipality of San Pedro as a component city of Laguna Province pursuant to Republic Act No. 10420 was ratified by in a plebiscite held for the purpose.

(I) Exercise general supervision and control over all progrants, projects, services, and activities of [he city government and in this connection, shall: xxx (v) Appoint all officials and employees whose salaries and wages are wholly or mainly paid out of city funds and whose åppointments are not otherwise provided for in this Code, as well as those he may be authorized by law to appoint;" [Emphasis supplied] It may be gleaned from the foregoing provision that the City Mayor's power to appoint only extends to "appointive" officials and employees whose appointments are not provided for by the Code or by law, i.e., Republic Act No. 10420, otherwise known as the "Charter of the City of San Pedro," as in this case. Note that the manner of filling-up permanent vacancies in the Office of the Local Chief Executive (LCE) and the sanggunian only applies under the circumstances enumerated under Section 44 of the Code, i.e., when an elective official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from office, voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office. While temporary vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive is filled-up under the circumstances enumerated under Section 46 of the Code, i.e., temporary incapacity in the performance of duties due to physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. Both presupposes that there is a duly elected public official holding a position who, due to a supervening event, was rendered permanent or temporarily incapacitated. Herein however, the supervening event is the creation of new barangays which brought about the creation of barangay elective positions for said barangays. As such, the manner of filling-up vacancies pursuant to Section 45 (a) (3)2, which authorizes the city mayor to appoint vacancies in the sangguniang barangay, cannot be made to apply herein. In view thereof, we regret to inform you that you do not have the authority to appoint/fill-up vacancies resulting from the Commission's denial of the city's request for the conduct of election of barangay officials for its newly created barangays. Commencement Existence of LGUs of Corporate In DILG Opinion No. 03, s. 2000, this Department opined that "since the corporate existence of the seven (7) newly-created barangays will begin only upon the election of 2 Section 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian — (a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automatic successions provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: The city or municipal mayor, in the case of sangguniang barangay, upon recommendation Of the sangguniang barangay concerned.

the barangay officials pursuant to Section 14 of the Local Government Code of 1991, the incumbent set of barangay elective officials of the mother barangay (Bgy. San Vicente) shall still continue in their respective offices until such time that the special election conducted and the respective Punong Barangay and a majority of the Members of the Sangguniang Barangay shall have been duly elected and qualified or until the expiration of their term of office, whichever comes earlier. " We find the foregoing applicable herein considering that Section 14 of the Code explicitly provides that the corporate existence of a new local government unit shall commence upon the election and qualification of its chief executive and a majority of the members of the sanggunian, unless some other time is fixed therefor by the law or ordinance creating it. Herein, Laguna Provincial Ordinance No. 8, s. 1997 does not contain any provision fixing the commencement of the newly-created barangays' corporate existence. As such, we sustain our opinion in DILG Opinion No. 03, s. 2000, that the seven (7) newly-created barangays shall remain under the control and supervision of the incumbent elective barangay officials of Barangay San Vicente, City of San Pedro, Laguna until the election and qualification of the respective barangay officials of the newly«reated barangays pursuant to Section 5 of said Ordinance. We to hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Dll.c„otJstG 201+120105 RD RENATO L. BRION DILG Region Brgy.
